title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for hyperglycemia.

HPI
The patient is a 58-year-old individual presenting for a follow-up visit regarding their type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient reports experiencing symptoms of hyperglycemia over the past month, including increased thirst and frequent urination. They have been taking their medications consistently but note that their blood glucose levels remain poorly controlled. The patient denies any recent changes to their activity level or significant changes in their daily routine.

Medication List
- Insulin (long-term)
- Metformin (long-term)

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. Physical examination reveals no acute distress. Skin is intact with no signs of infection. Vital signs are stable.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
2. Hyperglycemia.

Plan
We will continue the current regimen of insulin and metformin. The patient was instructed to monitor their blood glucose levels more frequently and keep a log for the next month. We will re-evaluate the dosage of the oral hypoglycemic medication at the next appointment to address the hyperglycemia. Follow-up in four weeks.
explanations: Diabetes documented as poorly controlled, out of control, or with hyperglycemia is coded to diabetes with hyperglycemia.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Hyperglycemia is a complication with its own code.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
